facts: Berlin describes Wohngeld as a housing-cost subsidy for people with low income that requires an application.
The amount depends on household members, eligible rent and total household income.
The responsible office is the Bürgeramt or Wohnungsamt in the applicant's district.
The service page lists WoGG § 22, WoGV and WoGVwV among the legal bases.
Kinderzuschlag is intended for families whose income covers the parents' own needs but not, or only narrowly, the whole family's needs.
Eligibility depends on factors including the child living in the household, receipt of Kindergeld, minimum income and household need.
The Familienportal identifies income, housing-cost and asset evidence among documents that can be required.
The official KiZ-Lotse can be used to check whether Kinderzuschlag may be relevant.
An online Kinderzuschlag application route is available after the pre-check.
BGB § 558 governs increases up to the local comparative rent under specified conditions.
The provision includes timing conditions and a capping limit, subject to the statutory details and exceptions.
A case-specific conclusion requires the landlord's stated legal basis, dates and property/local-rent facts.
Police guidance says acute threats should be reported via 110.
Existing digital material such as emails, chats, photos or videos can be important evidence and should preferably remain complete and unchanged until police contact.
A criminal complaint can be made at a police station; preserved evidence should be brought to the report.
Police guidance recommends preserving online evidence before it disappears.
A useful screenshot should preserve the relevant content, date/time, username, context, platform and associated URLs.
The guidance warns not to create screenshots of child or youth sexual-abuse material and instead to contact police.
Berlin's ServicePortal is the official directory for administrative services, locations and authorities.
Responsibility can be resolved through the specific service and location rather than inferred from an agency name alone.
Berlin IFG guidance describes a general right to request access to or information from authority records, subject to exceptions.
A request can be made to the body holding the records and should identify the relevant file or subject as clearly as possible.
Disclosure is not guaranteed because exclusions and costs can apply.
The Unternehmensregister provides access to register information from German register courts.
Available register outputs include current, chronological and historical extracts.
Chronological/historical evidence is useful for distinguishing current identity from past control or representation.
The Transparenzregister records information about beneficial owners for entities subject to transparency obligations.
Access is tiered; some users need to demonstrate a legitimate interest or another statutory access basis.
Beneficial ownership/control is a relationship question and should not be treated as proof that two legal entities are the same entity.
Bundeshaushalt digital provides interactive federal budget data across years, including expenditure/revenue and target/actual values where available.
Users can drill down through budget structure to individual titles.
The federal budget download portal provides public budget data and documents, including machine-readable CSV/XML for available years.
The portal states that the official budget document remains legally authoritative.
The Bundesrechnungshof publishes audit results including remarks, special reports and some final audit communications.
Audit reports can provide context for public-spending questions but do not replace recipient-level payment evidence.
Berlin's procurement platform publishes current public tenders and participation procedures.
The platform also links to publications about awarded contracts and other procurement notices.
Berlin publishes information about certain awarded contracts and intended restricted tenders through the procurement platform.
Repeated awards are observable procurement facts but require context before any inference about impropriety.
Berlin's tree-protection service identifies the district Umwelt- und Naturschutzamt as responsible based on the tree's location.
The service lists project/tree details, justification and a location plan among relevant application evidence.
The page lists BaumSchVO § 5 and other environmental legal bases.
Using public street land for a construction-site setup is a special use that requires a permit.
Berlin's service page lists an application for the construction-site area and a security deposit among requirements.
The service cites Berliner Straßengesetz § 11 among its legal bases.
Gesetze im Internet provides a near-daily update service pointing to newly promulgated federal provisions in the Bundesgesetzblatt.
The update service is available as an RSS feed.
The consolidated texts on Gesetze im Internet are not themselves the official promulgated version, so the underlying Bundesgesetzblatt document remains important for authoritative change evidence.
